display.purpose: Hero voice — 'It's a Match!', celebration headers, first-run welcome. Space Grotesk 700. May scale to ~72px for the match hero only.

headline.purpose: Section openers, empty-state headers, big stat moments. Space Grotesk 600.

title.purpose: Screen titles, recipe names, list section headers. Inter 600.

body.purpose: Ingredient lists, descriptions, settings rows. Inter 400-500. Cap measured prose at 65-75ch.

label.purpose: Chips, tab labels, metadata. Inter 600, sentence case — never tracked all-caps eyebrows.

numeral.purpose: Timers, 'card 7/20', streak counts, prep time, macros. JetBrains Mono 500 for scoreboard feel.

shadows.name: rest
shadows.purpose: Default. Surfaces sit on Canvas separated by a 1px ink@8% hairline — flat until touched.

shadows.name: raised
shadows.purpose: Sheets, active deck card at rest, floating controls. Soft, close, ambient.

shadows.name: lifted
shadows.purpose: Deck card mid-swipe and modals — 'in your hand' depth.

shadows.name: match-glow
shadows.purpose: Punch-Pink bloom behind the match card. The ONLY place glow is allowed.

motion.name: spring-cta
motion.purpose: Reanimated withSpring — CTA/press feedback (tactile press physics).

motion.name: reduced-motion-crossfade
motion.purpose: prefers-reduced-motion replacement for all match choreography.

narrative.overview: cookDaddy lives where a game cabinet meets a kitchen. The job is unserious — what's for dinner — but the payoff is real, so the interface plays like a well-built mobile game: confident color, big satisfying type, decisive tap targets, and reward beats that land. 'Arcade' supplies the energy and the game-feel; 'Kitchen' supplies the appetite and the warmth. The tension between the two is the brand. This system rejects generic recipe-app clutter, sterile productivity SaaS, and childish cartoonishness alike — playful is achieved through craft, never gimmicks. Color is committed: a single appetite-forward Persimmon carries identity across the whole app, not just the match overlay, so the product feels alive end to end rather than flat-until-payoff. Restraint guards potency — the loudest moment on any screen is reserved for the match.
keyCharacteristics: One bold brand color (Persimmon) used with intent across every surface, not hoarded for the overlay.
Big, confident display type (Space Grotesk) for moments; clean humanist body (Inter) for reading; mono numerals for arcade-scoreboard data.
One decision per screen — the deck and the match are the heroes; supporting surfaces stay quiet.
Tactile, spring-driven feedback: things you touch respond physically.
Reward only what's earned — matches celebrate; swipes whisper.

rules.name: The One Loud Thing Rule
rules.body: Each screen gets exactly one dominant color moment. If two things shout, neither is heard.

rules.name: The Earned-Pink Rule
rules.body: Punch Pink appears only on genuine reward (a match, a streak payoff). Its rarity is what makes the match feel electric.

rules.name: The Persimmon-Deep-on-Light Rule
rules.body: Base Persimmon (#F1582E) is ~3.4:1 on white and fails WCAG AA as text and behind white text. On light surfaces, Persimmon Deep (#CB4421, 4.74:1) carries anything text-bearing: primary-button fills with white labels, selected-chip fills, active-tab tint, primary links, and Persimmon-colored text. Reserve base #F1582E for non-text accents, borders, and fills behind >=24px display type. The AA bar is non-negotiable; when unsure, go deep.

rules.name: The No-Eyebrow Rule
rules.body: No tiny all-caps tracked kickers above sections. Hierarchy comes from size and weight, not decorative labels.

rules.name: The Mono-for-Numbers Rule
rules.body: Anything that ticks, counts, or scores is set in JetBrains Mono.

rules.name: The Flat-Until-Touched Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are flat at rest. Elevation is a response — to touch, to drag, to the match — never ambient decoration.

dos: Do carry Persimmon across the whole app (active tab, selected chip, primary CTA), so the product feels alive before the payoff.
Do keep one loud color moment per screen.
Do set anything that counts or ticks in JetBrains Mono.
Do make presses physical: spring-driven translate + color shift.
Do reserve Punch Pink, Spotlight, and Match Glow for the match moment only.
Do pair every success/danger signal with a glyph or label, and ship a prefers-reduced-motion alternative for every animation.
Do keep secondary text at Ink Muted or darker; verify >=4.5:1 against Canvas.
Do use Persimmon Deep (#CB4421) for any Persimmon that bears text or is an active tint on light (primary buttons, selected chips, active tab, links); base Persimmon #F1582E fails AA there.
donts: Don't ship generic recipe-app clutter — one decision per screen.
Don't drift into sterile productivity SaaS density.
Don't go childish or cartoonish — no mascots, balloon gradients, or comic-sans whimsy.
Don't use tiny all-caps tracked eyebrows above sections.
Don't round cards past 20px, and never pair a 1px border with a soft wide drop-shadow as decoration.
Don't rely on color alone for like/pass, success/error, or active tab.
Don't spend shadow on resting surfaces — flat until touched.
Don't let Danger Crimson and Persimmon read as the same signal; keep their hue separation.
